transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Devon Lee (Redwood Product), Liam O'Connor (Avalon Head of Search), Meera Patel (Avalon ML Eng), Oscar Ruiz (Avalon CTO), Nina Gomez (Avalon PM)

Summary:
Short demo/walkthrough of Redwood hosted embeddings + reranking endpoints, show Console usage and Optimize recommendations for their commerce search workload. Goal: confirm fit for a POC and gather requirements for performance SLOs and data-security constraints.

Topics discussed:
- Current stack (Avalon uses Elastic + custom reranker; looking for lower latency and improved relevance)
- Hosted API demo (embeddings endpoint, similarity search, reranker endpoint)
- Console: dataset uploads, evals, rerank tuning, rollout controls
- Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, quant profiles, caching)
- Security: SOC2, VPC/private plane, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
- Next steps and POC scoping

--- Transcript (timestamps approximated) ---
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan with Redwood, I'll run a quick agenda — Priya will do the technical demo.
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: Thanks — style, we have about 45 minutes? great. Our main thing is relevance for commerce searches, current reranker is heavy, costs are spiking.
[00:18] Priya Singh: Cool, hi all. Quick show of hands — you all saw the invite which called out embeddings + rerank? That's what I'll focus on, and then the Console/Optimize bits.
[00:25] Meera Patel: Yep, that's the core. We'll want to see accuracy improvement and latency numbers.
[00:30] Priya Singh: Perfect. Quick context: with the hosted API you call /embeddings to get vectors, then do a vector store nearest-neighbor lookup and call our /rerank endpoint with top-K candidates, the reranker is small transformer fine-tuned for pairwise scoring. We'll demo a live curl example.
[00:45] Devon Lee: Also show the Console where you can run evals against labeled NDCG sets and see token-level cost breakdowns.
[00:50] Oscar Ruiz: Important for us is security — we need SOC2, SSO, and optionally private control plane — are those available on hosted?
[00:58] Priya Singh: Hosted has SOC2, and for Private we offer VPC connectors and a private control plane. We'll share the whitepaper. For hosted we provide per-tenant isolation and audit logs; KMS integration is available for Private.
[01:10] Liam O'Connor: Cool. Can you start the demo — show embeddings similarity and the rerank flow?
[01:12] Priya Singh: Yep. I'm going to switch to a sandbox dataset — it's a small commerce catalog. First, a sample curl to generate an embedding: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-2-small","input":"waterproof hiking boots"}' — returns a 768-d vector.
[01:28] Meera Patel: Are embeddings normalized? we need consistent cosine sim pipelines.
[01:31] Priya Singh: They are L2-normalized by default, so cosine similarity works out of the box.
[01:36] [01:36] Priya Singh continued: Next step — we do a nearest neighbor search in your vector store. For the demo I'm using a built-in kNN in the Redwood Console to avoid third-party index plumbing. Top 10 hits come back in ~35 ms on our sandbox.
[01:50] Liam O'Connor: 35 ms for vector lookup — impressive. But our real traffic needs <50 ms end-to-end. How does rerank add latency?
[01:56] Priya Singh: Good question. The rerank call is per-query on the top-K, so there's an extra request to /rerank. For our hosted default model in this sandbox, rerank on top-10 adds ~18-40 ms depending on sequence length. We can push that down by using a smaller reranker or batching — which Redwood Optimize can recommend.
[02:16] Meera Patel: What's batching look like? do you batch at request level?
[02:19] Priya Singh: Two places to batch: embeddings request batching on the model serving layer, and rerank batching where we accumulate multiple user queries in micro-batches. For low-latency SLO we keep micro-batches small; Optimize analyzes traffic traces and suggests optimal batch sizes to balance cost/latency.
[02:34] Oscar Ruiz: And caching — can we cache top-replies for frequent queries?
[02:37] Priya Singh: Yes — Redwood provides prefix and KV cache for hot queries; the Console shows cache hit rates and suggests TTLs. It helped a previous retail customer cut token cost by 28%.
[02:47] [02:47] Devon Lee: Show Console — uploads dataset -> run eval -> results.
[02:50] Priya Singh: Switching screens, going into the Console. Here is the dataset tab, I upload the sample product titles and queries CSV. Then I create an evaluation with labeled relevances — we have a small NDCG test set. Running the eval... results: baseline nDCG@10 is 0.63, after enabling the reranker it's 0.78.
[03:18] Liam O'Connor: That's a tangible lift. How comparable is that in our catalog? our queries are lots of typos and brand-long tails.
[03:25] Priya Singh: We see similar gains on long-tail queries because the reranker takes context from the product description and query. We also support hybrid signals — you can include legacy signals as features into the reranker payload.
[03:36] Meera Patel: You mentioned hybrid — is that done client-side or do you send those signals to Redwood?
[03:40] Priya Singh: You can send them in the /rerank payload as numeric features; we don't require you to persist them. For hosted we recommend passing light-weight signals — e.g., click-through rate, price proximity — as part of the payload.
[03:52] Oscar Ruiz: A security quick question — audit logs, full-text retention? we can't keep PII in logs.
[03:58] Priya Singh: By default hosted anonymizes certain fields; for stricter controls we recommend Private with customer-managed retention and KMS. We'll share the retention configuration docs.
[04:08] [04:08] Jordan Kim: Quick interruption — competitors — how do you compare vs Algolia/Elastic?
[04:12] Liam O'Connor: yeah curious.
[04:13] Priya Singh: Short answer: Algolia/Elastic are great for classical retrieval and speed; Redwood focuses on combining dense embeddings and learned reranking to improve semantic relevance, with tooling for rollouts and observability. Also we expose cost/latency breakdown which many managed providers don't surface per-token.
[04:29] Nina Gomez: Any examples of quantization? we are looking to save cost on peak.
[04:33] Priya Singh: We support quantized model variants in Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we provide model variants optimized for cost — e.g., rwd-rank-compact which uses 4-bit quant and trades a point or two of nDCG for 40% cost savings. Optimize suggests which variant based on your evals.
[04:50] Meera Patel: Show an API example for rerank?
[04:53] Priya Singh: Absolutely. curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -d '{"model":"rwd-rank-1","query":"waterproof hiking boots","candidates":[{"id":"p1","text":"..."},{"id":"p2","text":"..."}],"features":{"ctr":0.12}}' — returns sorted candidates with scores and explain tokens.
[05:14] [05:14] Meera Patel: Explain tokens? like attention heatmaps?
[05:16] Priya Singh: We return per-token contribution scores (approx) that help triage why items were promoted. Not a full attention map but it's useful for debugging.
[05:25] Liam O'Connor: That helps our Product to justify moves. How do deployments/rollouts work? we want canary then full.
[05:30] Priya Singh: Console supports canary rollouts and A/B tests — you pick % traffic, compare evals and live metrics. Also automatic fallback to a cheaper model on high load.
[05:40] Oscar Ruiz: For POC we need an estimate: 1M queries/day, p95 latency <120 ms, budget target below $X (redacted on call) — can you meet that on hosted?
[05:52] Jordan Kim: We can. We'll size it — typically recommended is Dedicated for predictable cost at that scale, but we can start hosted and move to Dedicated. We'll include cost modeling in the follow-up.
[06:02] Meera Patel: In terms of integration effort, what do you see?
[06:06] Priya Singh: Typical path: 1) generate embeddings for your catalog, 2) index in your vector store or use Redwood's in-console index, 3) wire search layer to call rerank for top-K, 4) run evals and tune with Optimize. Average integration for a POC is 2-4 weeks with one engineer.
[06:20] Liam O'Connor: Can you run a quick live scenario — user searches "waterproof boots size 9" and show end-to-end?
[06:25] Priya Singh: Sure. Running query: embeddings call -> vector lookup -> top 10 -> rerank call. Live demo logs: embeddings 12 ms, vector lookup 28 ms, reranker 22 ms => total ~62 ms (demo env, not scaled).
[06:39] [06:39] Meera Patel: Sounds promising. Does Redwood support downstream closed-loop evals? like collecting signals and retraining?
[06:43] Priya Singh: We integrate with your analytics pipeline — Console can capture clicks and we'll surface drift alerts; for retraining pipelines we provide export hooks and evaluation wrappers.
[06:52] Nina Gomez: For compliance — have you done any ecomm clients in EU? we need data residency.
[06:57] Priya Singh: Yes, we have EU regions and can pin hosted tooling to eu-west. For stricter residency we recommend Private.
[07:05] Liam O'Connor: Pricing follow-up: can you show a quick model of cost per 1M queries?
[07:10] Jordan Kim: We'll send a tailored sheet but rough math: embeddings + retrieval is low cost, rerank is the main token cost. With compact reranker variants and caching you can hit your budget target; we'll model both hosted and Dedicated.
[07:22] Oscar Ruiz: Any limitations on candidate size? we typically pass 50 candidates then rerank to top 10.
[07:27] Priya Singh: We support candidate lists up to 200, but per-call latency and cost increases; Optimize will recommend K based on your traffic and latency SLOs.
[07:37] Meera Patel: We also use product attributes heavily — price, brand. Can we tune weights?
[07:41] Priya Singh: Yes — you can pass attributes as features and train the reranker to incorporate them; also use ensemble scoring in the Console.
[07:50] Jordan Kim: Quick note — I'll attach a demo notebook, sample curl scripts, and a short checklist for the POC.
[07:55] Liam O'Connor: Perfect. One last question — latency at 95th when rerank is used heavily under load — do you have mitigation?
[07:59] Priya Singh: Mitigations: 1) model fallback to cheaper variant, 2) regional routing to less loaded instance, 3) increase batch windows for non-critical paths, 4) TTL cache for repeated queries. All configurable via policies.
[08:12] [08:12] Nina Gomez: Onboarding — who will be our contact?
[08:15] Jordan Kim: I'll be the AE and Priya SE lead. We'll assign a Solutions Engineer for the POC.
[08:20] Meera Patel: Ok let's talk POC goals — Meera outlines: improve nDCG@10 by 0.12, keep p95 <120ms, cost delta <20% on monthly run.
[08:32] Meera Patel: I'll send sample queries and a small labelled set.
[08:35] Jordan Kim: Great. We'll aim to have a detailed POC plan in the follow-up and pricing sheet.
[08:40] Oscar Ruiz: Thanks everyone.
[08:42] Jordan Kim: Thanks, we'll follow up with docs and next steps.

End of transcript.
